query: For initially solid FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles exposed to the premelting and melting regime, the limited understanding of their thermal response prevents clear definition of their usable temperature range and behavior during high-temperature synthesis. What single testable mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the onset and progression of their phase transition and why? Specify a controlled comparison, predicted observations relative to the starting baseline, relevant boundary conditions, supporting evidence from prior nanoparticle studies, and a result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles (HEA-NPs) of 10–20 nm diameter, the onset and radial progression of premelting/melting are governed by copper‐rich surface segregation: Cu atoms diffuse to the surface on heating, locally lowering the cohesive energy and initiating surface premelting; continued Cu flux sustains an inward, layer-by-layer melting front. If Cu surface segregation is kinetically suppressed, the premelting onset temperature will increase and the melting transition will sharpen.
generation.material_initial_state: Equiatomic FeNiCrCoCu nanoparticles, 10–20 nm, single-phase fcc, chemically homogeneous immediately after rapid quench from 900 °C, ligand-free surfaces, stored under Ar.
generation.intervention: Create two populations: (A) allow natural surface relaxation (1 h at 200 °C, Ar) to promote Cu surface segregation; (B) immediately coat particles with a 2 nm SiO2 shell at room temperature to kinetically block surface diffusion/segregation.
generation.conditions: Heat both populations from 300 K to 1300 K at 10 K min⁻¹ in high-vacuum in an in-situ TEM with simultaneous nanobeam electron diffraction; no oxidation (≤10⁻⁷ Torr O₂).
generation.structural_mediator: Cu-enriched 1–2 nm surface shell (population A) versus chemically frozen surface (population B).
generation.mechanism: Cu atoms possess the lowest cohesive energy among the five constituents and preferentially occupy surface sites. Their enrichment reduces local bonding strength and surface energy, decreasing the thermodynamic barrier for surface premelting. Once a disordered liquid layer forms, the chemical potential gradient drives further Cu diffusion to the interface, perpetuating radial melting toward the core.
generation.predicted_outcome: Population A will exhibit (i) initial diffuse intensity loss and liquid-like halo in diffraction starting at T_on ≈ 850 ± 25 K, and (ii) gradual inward melting over a ∼150 K interval. Population B will retain sharp diffraction until T_on,B ≈ 1000 ± 25 K (≥150 K higher) and transform to liquid within ≤25 K, showing an abrupt transition. Differential scanning calorimetry would record an earlier, broader endothermic event for A and a later, sharper peak for B.
generation.baseline: Untreated FeNiCrCoCu HEA-NPs (population A) begin premelting at ≈850 K under identical heating, consistent with prior reports for 10–20 nm Cu-containing HEA NPs.
generation.boundary: Particle diameters 5–30 nm; inert or high-vacuum atmosphere; negligible oxidation; heating rates ≤20 K min⁻¹. Outside this (larger particles, oxidizing atmosphere, very fast ramps) additional factors (surface stress, oxide formation) may dominate, invalidating the prediction.
generation.uncertainty: Magnitude of the T_on shift (estimated ~150 K) may vary with exact particle size and coating integrity; other segregation processes (e.g., Ni) could partly compensate, altering the effect.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform identical in-situ TEM heating experiments on populations A and B, recording electron diffraction patterns and real-time imaging to track onset and propagation of melting.
measurements: Onset temperature where crystalline diffraction intensity drops to 90 % of initial
Temperature interval over which complete disappearance of Bragg spots occurs
Chemical mapping (EELS/EDS) of surface vs core before and after heating to confirm Cu redistribution
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: The hypothesis is falsified if population B (Cu-segregation-suppressed) shows the same or lower premelting onset temperature (within ±25 K) and equally broad transition width as population A, or if no measurable Cu surface enrichment is detected in population A before heating.
